correctness.rationale: Standard complete classification of all 240 exceptional curves supplies eight blow-up divisors (away from Q) and 232 plane multiplicity classes. General position of both eight-point sets is checked. The attached standalone standard-library checker exhausts all 232 classes per example, giving 225 augmented jet matrices of full column rank modulo 1000003. Each such full rank proves characteristic-zero nonexistence of the corresponding class through Q. For exactly seven classes, exact rational one-dimensional kernels give vanishing value at Q and nonzero, pairwise nonproportional tangent gradients. This establishes exactly seven smooth transverse branches of the full reduced divisor, with delta=21, Milnor=36 by the standard formula. The non-torsion property itself is properly attributed to the primary paper. Computation terminates with explicit VERIFY_OK and is a complete finite mathematical certificate, not statistical evidence.

Primary Theorem 2.1 and Section 5 abstract cliques do not imply exact local incidence. Semantically focused published-finding corpus queries and the published literature comparison found no implication-equivalent result; unindexed treatments remain a bibliographic risk.
residual_risks: An older thesis or unindexed auxiliary source might already compute exact marked incidences; source statement of seven examples might informally intend exactness without exhibiting exhaustive evidence.
No claim of unpublished-work uniqueness follows from database searches or mathematical partitioning.

value.rationale: The 2022 source studies the threshold between known seven-curve non-torsion examples and the still-open eight-curve non-torsion case. At both of its principal explicit examples the natural exact invariant is the number of all geometric exceptional curves containing its distinguished non-torsion point, not merely the seven exhibited examples. The full 240-class exclusion and ordinary septuple local type with delta/Milnor invariants resolve both natural marked configurations completely and rule out hidden eighth components. The result does not pretend to solve the general eightfold problem.
